transcript.text: I've uploaded customers.csv. Please build a leakage-safe baseline churn classifier on churned_next_month (logistic regression vs gradient boosting), split by signup_date with the latest 20% as holdout, and report precision at the top 200. Our 4-person retention team can call 200 customers a month; I need this baseline before I build my own model. [shares customers.csv]

Your build request is recorded and the build starts now. What I checked first: the table has 1,200 rows and 8 columns, churned_next_month runs at a base rate of **17.4%**, and the leakage check flagged no column written after the outcome — nothing to drop. DCLab will now train logistic regression and gradient boosting, split by signup_date with the latest 20% held out, and score both on how many churners land in the top 200 of the risk ranking. The base rate is the yardstick: a model is only worth calling people over if it finds more churners in those 200 slots than an unranked draw would. One thing I assumed: tenure_months, monthly_spend and support_tickets_90d are read as of the scoring date, not refreshed after someone churns. Tell me if any of them are backfilled from later records and I'll have them dropped.
